_comment: Checklist config for the UX review agent (ux_review.py, invoked via /ux-review on a PR). Two kinds of checks: 'deterministic_rules' are mechanical pattern checks run in Python (no LLM); 'llm_rubric' drives the judgment-based pass sent to the model. Edit this file to tune the review without touching code. Severity order for the ranked output is defined by 'severity_order'.

deterministic_rules.message: README does not include the shared memory-configuration step. Nearly every Lemonade/GPU playbook opens with '## Setting the Memory Configuration' followed by '<!-- @require:memory-config -->'. Add it unless this playbook genuinely has no memory-pool requirement.

Found a legacy '@setup:memory_config' style tag. The correct, injected form is '@require:memory-config' (hyphen, @require). The @setup form is mis-parsed by the test runner and the memory-config content will not render.

The '@require:software-update' block should be wrapped in a '<!-- @device:halo_box -->' / '<!-- @device:end -->' scope, matching sibling playbooks (the Developer Center software-update flow is halo_box-specific).

This playbook installs/uses podman but also invokes 'docker run'. On a fresh AMD system that followed the podman steps, 'docker' may not exist. Use 'podman run' (or note that docker can be aliased to podman).
A shell command line appears to end with a stray backtick, which will cause the shell to hang or error on copy-paste. Remove the trailing backtick.
A user-level systemd unit (managed with 'systemctl --user') is being edited with 'sudo', which creates a root-owned file the user service cannot manage. Drop 'sudo'.
playbook.json is missing one or more expected fields.

The README contains '@os:windows' content, but playbook.json does not list 'windows' under supported_platforms for any device. That Windows content will never render on the site. Either add Windows support in playbook.json or remove/relocate the Windows-only content.

This playbook runs a large model but may not remind low-memory / low-VRAM devices to pick a smaller one. If small-VRAM devices are in supported_platforms, add a 'choose a smaller model if your hardware lacks memory' note at the run command.
Large model downloads happen on first run but there may be no note setting that expectation. Consider a brief 'the first run downloads the model, which can take a while' note.

categories.prompt: Are the instructions clear and unambiguous for a first-time user? Flag steps that assume unstated context, reference a UI element or path without saying where it is, or could be misread.
Is anything needlessly wordy or repeated? Flag redundant sentences, filler, or over-explanation. Do not recommend removing safety/disclaimer content.
Does this playbook follow the conventions of the others: section ordering (memory config early, prerequisites, numbered steps), heading style, tone, and tag usage? Flag deviations.
Flag grammar, spelling, capitalization, and punctuation errors, including mid-sentence capitalization and malformed lists.

Flag anything that would break on copy-paste or mislead the user: commands that won't run as written, wrong ports/paths, self-contradictory values, advice that is a no-op, or version/number claims that contradict other parts of the doc.

Are appropriate caveats present where needed: hardware/memory requirements, untested or unofficial steps flagged as such, autonomous-agent risk warnings, and machine-specific assumptions? Flag missing or overstated claims (e.g. asserting a hard failure threshold that was never verified).

llm_rubric.instructions: You are a documentation UX reviewer for AMD Ryzen AI Halo playbooks. Review ONLY the changed playbook provided. For each issue, give: a one-line title, the severity (correctness, consistency, or polish), a short explanation, and where possible the specific line or snippet. Do not rewrite the whole document. Do not invent problems; if a category is clean, say nothing for it. Prefer a small number of high-value findings over an exhaustive nitpick list. Never recommend removing safety, disclaimer, or licensing content.
